issues.description: The Solution's PersonResource constructor signature and initialization do not match the Template and the expectations in the problem statement. The template and the exercise expect PersonResource to be constructed with a PersonService and to assign it to the personService field so the controller methods can call personService. In the solution, the constructor incorrectly accepts a NoteService and sets personService to null, which will cause a NullPointerException at runtime and contradicts the intended dependency injection structure.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the solution to accept PersonService and assign it to the personService field, matching the template and enabling dependency injection. Example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }

issues.description: PersonResource constructor in the solution repository takes a NoteService parameter and assigns null to the personService field, while the template and the problem statement clearly expect PersonResource to depend on PersonService. This mismatch between the constructor parameter type/name and the intended PersonService dependency breaks the conceptual mapping (the resource for managing persons should accept a PersonService) and will confuse students when comparing template, problem description, and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the PersonResource constructor in the solution to accept a PersonService parameter and assign it to the personService field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } This restores consistent naming and correct dependency injection for the PersonResource.
